first.rationale: The competitor's aggressive entry pricing is actively pulling price-sensitive SMB accounts, making promotional pricing the most directly responsive lever this week. Memory_73 supports this with prior acquisition/revenue lift and reduced time-to-first-value for the same segment, but it was consolidated under different competitive conditions, so I want the archived record verified before committing capacity. I also verify memory_31 because onboarding/activation declines are simultaneous and could stem from a different root cause (friction, not price) — if verification shows the onboarding effect was stronger or more durable, that could override this choice. Given the primary objective is sustainable qualified revenue rather than raw acquisition, I flag risk that promotional pricing could attract lower-quality, more churn-prone accounts, so I'm running this as a small guarded test rather than a broad rollout, preserving the ability to pivot toward onboarding/activation fixes next cycle if margin or retention signals look weak.
